Prioritize findings based on exploitability and asset sensitivity.

Thousands of unprioritized alerts do not improve security.

---

topics.title: Appendix DA — Security Baselines
topics.markdown:
Baseline controls:

- MFA
- no root/admin daily use
- centralized audit
- encrypted storage
- private DB
- backup
- vulnerability scanning
- secret management

Automate these into landing zone.

---

topics.title: Appendix DB — Cloud Threat Modeling
keyPoints: What if CI pipeline is compromised?
What if storage policy is wrong?
topics.markdown:
Identify:

- assets
- actors
- trust boundaries
- entry points
- data flows

Ask:

- What if account credential leaks?
- What if workload is compromised?
- What if CI pipeline is compromised?
- What if storage policy is wrong?

---

topics.title: Appendix DC — Cloud Supply Chain Security
topics.markdown:
Cloud supply chain includes:

- source code
- dependencies
- build runners
- container registry
- IaC modules
- deployment credentials

Protect the path from commit to production.

---

topics.title: Appendix DD — CI/CD Identity
topics.summary: CI should use short-lived federated credentials where possible.
topics.markdown:
CI should use short-lived federated credentials where possible.

Avoid storing permanent cloud admin keys in CI secrets.

Scope deployment roles per environment.

---

topics.title: Appendix DE — Environment Separation
topics.summary: Production should have stronger isolation from:
topics.markdown:
Production should have stronger isolation from:

- developer laptops
- development credentials
- test data

Separate accounts/projects reduce accidental cross-environment actions.

---

topics.title: Appendix DF — Centralized Audit Account
topics.summary: Security logs stored separately prevent application administrators from easily deleting evidence.
topics.markdown:
Security logs stored separately prevent application administrators from easily deleting evidence.

Use restricted access and immutable retention where appropriate.

---

topics.title: Appendix DG — Encryption in Transit
topics.markdown:
Encrypt:

- public traffic
- service-to-service
- database connections
- hybrid links

Use modern TLS.

Do not disable validation to bypass certificate problems.

---

topics.title: Appendix DH — Egress Filtering
topics.summary: Restrict outbound destinations for sensitive workloads.
topics.markdown:
Restrict outbound destinations for sensitive workloads.

Benefits:

- reduce exfiltration
- block command-and-control

Costs:

- maintenance
- third-party IP/domain changes

Use proxies/domain-aware controls where needed.

---

topics.title: Appendix DI — WAF Rule Tuning
topics.markdown:
Too strict:

- false positives

Too loose:

- limited protection

Monitor in detection/count mode before enforcing high-risk rules when possible.

---

topics.title: Appendix DJ — Rate Limiting at Edge
topics.summary: Edge throttling protects origin before traffic consumes application resources.
topics.markdown:
Edge throttling protects origin before traffic consumes application resources.

Use different limits for:

- anonymous
- authenticated
- expensive endpoints

But application may still need per-business-account limits.

---

topics.title: Appendix DK — Audit Trail
topics.markdown:
Record:

- who changed infrastructure
- what changed
- when
- source
- result

Cloud control-plane audit is critical for incident response.

---

topics.title: Appendix DL — Infrastructure Change Approval
topics.summary: Not every change needs manual approval.
topics.markdown:
Not every change needs manual approval.

Automate low-risk changes.

Require stronger review for:

- network core
- IAM
- key policy
- production database
- global traffic

Risk-based controls scale better than universal bureaucracy.

---

topics.title: Appendix DM — Policy as Code
codeBlocks:
deny public bucket
deny unencrypted database
require owner tag
deny public SSH
topics.markdown:
Examples:

```text
deny public bucket
deny unencrypted database
require owner tag
deny public SSH
```

Run in:

- CI
- admission control
- cloud organization policy

---

topics.title: Appendix DN — Terraform State Security
topics.markdown:
State can contain:

- resource IDs
- configuration
- sometimes sensitive values

Protect:

- encryption
- IAM
- locking
- backups

Do not expose state broadly.

---

topics.title: Appendix DO — Terraform Module Versioning
topics.summary: Shared modules should use explicit versions.
topics.markdown:
Shared modules should use explicit versions.

Breaking a module used by 500 stacks can cause wide impact.

Use:

- semantic releases
- changelog
- migration guide
- compatibility

---

topics.title: Appendix DP — Terraform Import
topics.markdown:
Import existing resources carefully.

Import only maps resource to state; configuration still needs to match actual resource.

Run plan and resolve drift.

---

topics.title: Appendix DQ — Terraform Destroy Risk
topics.summary: Production destroy permissions should be tightly controlled.
topics.markdown:
Production destroy permissions should be tightly controlled.

Use:

- protected resources
- deletion prevention
- backups
- review

Automation can delete infrastructure faster than humans can react.

---

topics.title: Appendix DR — IaC Dependency Graphs
topics.summary: Declarative tools infer dependency from references.
topics.markdown:
Declarative tools infer dependency from references.

Manual `depends_on`-style controls should be used only when dependency is real but implicit.

Too many explicit dependencies reduce parallelism and clarity.

---

topics.title: Appendix DS — Drift Detection
topics.markdown:
Run scheduled plan/diff.

Classify drift:

- authorized emergency change
- provider-managed mutation
- accidental console change

Reconcile deliberately.

---

topics.title: Appendix DT — GitOps Reconciliation Risk
topics.summary: A GitOps controller can rapidly reapply a bad state.
topics.markdown:
A GitOps controller can rapidly reapply a bad state.

Use:

- staged promotion
- policy checks
- protected branches
- progressive rollout

Automation amplifies both good and bad changes.

---

topics.title: Appendix DU — Deployment Artifact Immutability
codeBlocks:
dev
 -> staging
 -> production
topics.markdown:
Build once.

Promote same artifact:

```text
dev
 -> staging
 -> production
```

Do not rebuild source separately for production and hope it is identical.

---

topics.title: Appendix DV — Blue/Green Cloud Deployment
codeBlocks:
Blue = current
Green = new
topics.markdown:
Two environments:

```text
Blue = current
Green = new
```

Switch traffic.

Benefits:

- easy rollback

Costs:

- duplicate capacity
- database compatibility

---

topics.title: Appendix DW — Canary Deployment
topics.markdown:
Route:

```text
1%
5%
25%
50%
100%
```

Observe:

- error rate
- latency
- business metrics

Automate stop if regression.

---

topics.title: Appendix DX — Shadow Traffic
topics.summary: Duplicate real requests to new system but do not use response.
topics.markdown:
Duplicate real requests to new system but do not use response.

Useful for:

- performance
- correctness comparison

Prevent side effects in shadow path.

---

topics.title: Appendix DY — Rollback and Data
topics.summary: Code rollback may be unsafe if new version wrote incompatible data.
topics.markdown:
Code rollback may be unsafe if new version wrote incompatible data.

Use expand/contract migrations.

Sometimes roll-forward is safer.

---

topics.title: Appendix DZ — Infrastructure Rollback
topics.summary: Infrastructure rollback may not be simple:
topics.markdown:
Infrastructure rollback may not be simple:

- deleted data
- changed DNS
- rotated key
- recreated DB

Design reversibility before applying.

---

topics.title: Appendix EA — Logs as a Cost Center
topics.markdown:
Logging cost can include:

- ingestion
- storage
- search
- export

Reduce:

- noisy success logs
- giant payloads
- long retention

Do not remove necessary audit/security logs to save money.

---

topics.title: Appendix EB — Metrics Cardinality
codeBlocks:
user_id
request_id
full URL

route
status
region
service
topics.markdown:
Labels such as:

```text
user_id
request_id
full URL
```

can explode costs.

Use bounded dimensions:

```text
route
status
region
service
```

---

topics.title: Appendix EC — Trace Sampling
topics.markdown:
Strategies:

- head sampling
- tail sampling
- error-biased sampling

Keep enough traces for rare failures.

---

topics.title: Appendix ED — Cloud Audit Log Retention
topics.summary: Control-plane audit logs often need longer retention than debug logs.
topics.markdown:
Control-plane audit logs often need longer retention than debug logs.

Protect them separately.

---

topics.title: Appendix EE — Multi-Region Observability
topics.markdown:
Dashboards should compare regions:

- traffic
- error
- latency
- replication lag
- capacity

A regional failure may look healthy in global average.

---

topics.title: Appendix EF — Synthetic Monitoring
topics.summary: Run synthetic user paths from multiple geographies:
codeBlocks:
DNS
login
API
DB write
read
topics.markdown:
Run synthetic user paths from multiple geographies:

```text
DNS
login
API
DB write
read
```

Detect problems external to service metrics.

---

topics.title: Appendix EG — Business Monitoring
topics.markdown:
Monitor:

- orders
- payments
- signups
- file processing success

Technical metrics can be green while product logic is broken.

---

topics.title: Appendix EH — SLO by User Journey
codeBlocks: checkout success
VM uptime
topics.markdown:
Prefer:

```text
checkout success
```

over:

```text
VM uptime
```

User-centric SLOs align architecture with business.

---

topics.title: Appendix EI — Multi-AZ Capacity Math
topics.summary: If you operate across 3 AZs and require surviving 1 AZ loss:
topics.markdown:
If you operate across 3 AZs and require surviving 1 AZ loss:

Each remaining 2 AZs must together handle full traffic.

Normal capacity should leave headroom.

---

topics.title: Appendix EJ — Failure Capacity
topics.summary: A system designed to use 95% of every resource during normal traffic has little resilience.
topics.markdown:
A system designed to use 95% of every resource during normal traffic has little resilience.

Plan spare capacity for:

- AZ failure
- deployments
- bursts
- maintenance

---

topics.title: Appendix EK — Region Evacuation
topics.markdown:
A multi-region system should test:

- remove one region from traffic
- fail database writer
- restore capacity elsewhere
- validate secrets
- validate queues

Hidden regional dependencies are common.

---

topics.title: Appendix EL — DR Tiering
codeBlocks:
Tier 0: identity, payments, routing
Tier 1: core APIs
Tier 2: notifications
Tier 3: analytics
topics.markdown:
Classify workloads:

```text
Tier 0: identity, payments, routing
Tier 1: core APIs
Tier 2: notifications
Tier 3: analytics
```

Not every service needs same RTO/RPO.

---

topics.title: Appendix EM — Backup vs Replication
topics.markdown:
Replication protects availability.

Backup protects from logical destruction.

If production deletes every row, replication can faithfully copy deletion.

Need both.

---

topics.title: Appendix EN — Immutable Backups
topics.summary: Keep protected backup copy outside normal production credentials.
topics.markdown:
Keep protected backup copy outside normal production credentials.

Useful against:

- ransomware
- accidental mass deletion
- compromised administrator

---

topics.title: Appendix EO — Point-In-Time Recovery
topics.summary: PITR can restore database to time before logical corruption.
topics.markdown:
PITR can restore database to time before logical corruption.

Plan:

- target time
- isolated restore
- validation
- traffic cutover
- downstream reconciliation

---

topics.title: Appendix EP — Restore Drills
topics.markdown:
Test:

- backup availability
- key access
- actual restore time
- application compatibility

Measure RTO, do not guess it.

---

topics.title: Appendix EQ — Failover Fencing
topics.summary: When promoting secondary, prevent old primary from accepting writes.
topics.markdown:
When promoting secondary, prevent old primary from accepting writes.

Otherwise split brain.

Use provider-supported fencing/consensus mechanisms.

---

topics.title: Appendix ER — Failback Data Reconciliation
keyPoints: ensure old region has latest state
topics.markdown:
Before moving back:

- synchronize
- compare data
- verify replication
- ensure old region has latest state

Failback without validation can reintroduce stale data.

---

topics.title: Appendix ES — Active-Active Conflict Resolution
topics.markdown:
Possible:

- last-write-wins
- application merge
- home-region ownership
- conflict-free data type
- globally coordinated transaction

Choose based on domain.

"Just replicate both ways" is not a conflict strategy.

---

topics.title: Appendix ET — Home Region Pattern
topics.markdown:
Assign entity/tenant a home region.

Writes go there.

Reads may be global.

Benefits:

- avoids multi-writer conflict
- supports residency

Requires routing metadata and migration process.

---

topics.title: Appendix EU — Global Session Design
topics.markdown:
Sessions may be:

- region-local
- globally replicated
- token-based

Trade-offs:

- latency
- failover
- revocation

Design session behavior during region loss.

---

topics.title: Appendix EV — Global Identity Dependency
topics.summary: If all regions synchronously call one identity service in one region, you do not have regional independence.
topics.markdown:
If all regions synchronously call one identity service in one region, you do not have regional independence.

Cache validation keys and design local token verification where appropriate.

---

topics.title: Appendix EW — Regionalized Dependencies
topics.summary: Map every critical dependency by region:
codeBlocks:
App
DB
Cache
Queue
Secrets
KMS
Registry
DNS
Identity
topics.markdown:
Map every critical dependency by region:

```text
App
DB
Cache
Queue
Secrets
KMS
Registry
DNS
Identity
```

A single non-replicated dependency defeats multi-region claims.

---

topics.title: Appendix EX — Chaos in Cloud
topics.markdown:
Test realistic cloud failures:

- IAM deny
- AZ node loss
- DNS failure
- KMS access denial
- network latency
- quota throttle

Not only `kill -9` a process.

---

topics.title: Appendix EY — Provider Outage Strategy
topics.markdown:
You cannot prevent provider outage.

Choose:

- tolerate
- multi-region
- multi-cloud

based on business impact.

Multi-cloud DR may be far more expensive than accepting a rare region outage.

---

topics.title: Appendix EZ — Provider API Throttling
topics.markdown:
Control-plane APIs have rate limits.

Bulk provisioning may hit throttling.

Use:

- exponential backoff
- batching
- staged operations

Do not create thousands of resources in a tight loop without limits.

---

topics.title: Appendix FA — Quota Runway
codeBlocks: used / quota

85% IP addresses used
growth 2%/week
topics.markdown:
Track:

```text
used / quota
```

and projected growth.

Example:

```text
85% IP addresses used
growth 2%/week
```

Act before deployment failure.

---

topics.title: Appendix FB — IP Exhaustion
topics.summary: Kubernetes and private endpoints can consume many IPs.
topics.markdown:
Kubernetes and private endpoints can consume many IPs.

Symptoms:

- pods cannot schedule
- endpoints cannot create

Plan address space early.

---

topics.title: Appendix FC — DNS Query Limits
topics.markdown:
Resolvers/services can have quotas.

Highly chatty applications that resolve DNS for every request can cause needless load.

Reuse connections.

---

topics.title: Appendix FD — Connection Reuse
topics.markdown:
Long-lived clients should reuse:

- TCP
- TLS
- DB connections

Benefits:

- lower latency
- lower CPU
- reduced NAT ports

---

topics.title: Appendix FE — Cross-Zone Data Transfer Cost
topics.markdown:
Some providers charge cross-zone transfer.

Architecture that constantly crosses AZs may have hidden cost.

Balance:

- resilience
- locality
- cost

Do not compromise HA solely to avoid small transfer cost without analysis.

---

topics.title: Appendix FF — Cross-Region Cost
topics.summary: Cross-region replication and APIs can be expensive.
codeBlocks: bytes/sec × price × month
topics.markdown:
Cross-region replication and APIs can be expensive.

Measure:

```text
bytes/sec × price × month
```

Global architecture has recurring network economics.

---

topics.title: Appendix FG — NAT Cost
topics.markdown:
Managed NAT can charge:

- hourly
- per GB

Large object downloads through NAT may be unnecessarily expensive.

Use private endpoints or direct paths where appropriate.

---

topics.title: Appendix FH — Idle Resource Cost
topics.markdown:
Common waste:

- dev clusters running nights/weekends
- unattached disks
- old snapshots
- idle load balancers
- oversized DBs
- unused public IPs

Automate cleanup.

---

topics.title: Appendix FI — Cost Anomaly Detection
topics.summary: Alert when service spend deviates significantly from baseline.
topics.markdown:
Alert when service spend deviates significantly from baseline.

Possible causes:

- traffic spike
- logging bug
- loop
- compromised credential
- forgotten resource

Cost is an operational signal.

---

topics.title: Appendix FJ — Budget Guardrails
topics.summary: Budgets can notify, but hard shutdown on budget limit may be dangerous for production.
topics.markdown:
Budgets can notify, but hard shutdown on budget limit may be dangerous for production.

Use environment-specific policies.

Development can be aggressively capped.

Production requires controlled response.

---

topics.title: Appendix FK — Unit Economics
codeBlocks:
cost / active tenant
cost / transaction
cost / GB processed
topics.markdown:
For SaaS:

```text
cost / active tenant
cost / transaction
cost / GB processed
```

helps compare architecture choices.

---

topics.title: Appendix FL — Reserved vs On-Demand Economics
topics.markdown:
Stable baseline:

- commitments can reduce cost

Variable burst:

- on-demand/spot

Portfolio should match workload shape.

---

topics.title: Appendix FM — Autoscaling and Cost
topics.markdown:
Autoscaling can reduce idle cost.

But scale-to-zero can increase cold-start latency.

Choose based on SLO.

---

topics.title: Appendix FN — FinOps Ownership
topics.summary: Teams should see cost for the systems they design.
topics.markdown:
Teams should see cost for the systems they design.

Central FinOps provides:

- tools
- rates
- standards

Engineering teams act on optimization.

---

topics.title: Appendix FO — SaaS Tenant Metering
topics.markdown:
Meter usage:

- API calls
- storage
- compute
- seats
- messages

Metering itself must be:

- reliable
- auditable
- idempotent

Billing errors are customer trust issues.

---

topics.title: Appendix FP — Tenant Quotas
topics.summary: Use quotas to control noisy neighbors.
topics.markdown:
Use quotas to control noisy neighbors.

Examples:

- RPS
- storage
- concurrent jobs

Return explicit quota errors.

---

topics.title: Appendix FQ — Dedicated Tenants
topics.markdown:
Large/regulatory tenants may get:

- dedicated DB
- dedicated cluster
- dedicated account

This increases isolation and cost.

Automate provisioning.

---

topics.title: Appendix FR — Tenant Routing
codeBlocks: tenant -> region -> cell -> database
topics.markdown:
Maintain mapping:

```text
tenant -> region -> cell -> database
```

Routing data becomes critical control-plane state.

Cache with last-known-good behavior.

---

topics.title: Appendix FS — Tenant Migration
topics.markdown:
Move tenant:

1. copy data
2. capture changes
3. validate
4. pause/switch writes
5. update routing
6. verify
7. clean old

Make operation restartable.

---

topics.title: Appendix FT — Cell-Based Architecture
codeBlocks:
LB
App
Cache
DB
Queue
topics.markdown:
A cell is independent slice:

```text
LB
App
Cache
DB
Queue
```

serving subset of tenants.

Benefits:

- bounded blast radius
- horizontal scale

Requires tenant/cell routing.

---

topics.title: Appendix FU — Cell Failure
topics.summary: If one cell fails, only its tenants should be impacted.
topics.markdown:
If one cell fails, only its tenants should be impacted.

This is stronger isolation than one global database.

At very large scale, cells are powerful.

---

topics.title: Appendix FV — Cloud Migration Discovery
topics.markdown:
Inventory:

- servers
- databases
- integrations
- DNS
- certificates
- batch jobs
- file shares
- cron
- licensing

Hidden dependencies break migrations.

---

topics.title: Appendix FW — Dependency Mapping
codeBlocks:
App A -> DB A
App A -> App B
App B -> mainframe
topics.markdown:
Build graph:

```text
App A -> DB A
App A -> App B
App B -> mainframe
```

Migrate by dependency groups/waves.

---

topics.title: Appendix FX — Migration Wave Planning
topics.markdown:
Group workloads by:

- dependencies
- business criticality
- complexity
- team readiness

Start with representative low-risk workloads.

---

topics.title: Appendix FY — Rehost
topics.markdown:
Move VM mostly unchanged.

Pros:

- fast

Cons:

- carries old architecture/cost

Useful as interim step.

---

topics.title: Appendix FZ — Replatform
codeBlocks: VM DB -> managed DB
topics.markdown:
Change some components:

```text
VM DB -> managed DB
```

without rewriting whole application.

Often provides good value/risk balance.

---

topics.title: Appendix GA — Refactor
topics.markdown:
Change architecture deeply.

Use for systems where:

- scaling
- reliability
- velocity

justify investment.

Do not refactor everything during initial migration.

---

topics.title: Appendix GB — Retire
topics.summary: Some applications should be deleted rather than migrated.
topics.markdown:
Some applications should be deleted rather than migrated.

Cloud migration is an opportunity to reduce portfolio.

---

topics.title: Appendix GC — Retain
topics.markdown:
Some systems may remain on-prem:

- hardware dependency
- latency
- regulation
- end-of-life soon

Cloud strategy can intentionally include retained systems.

---

topics.title: Appendix GD — Repurchase
topics.markdown:
Replace custom system with SaaS.

Evaluate:

- migration
- customization
- integration
- vendor risk
- recurring cost

---

topics.title: Appendix GE — Migration Cutover
topics.markdown:
Before cutover:

- replication caught up
- test complete
- DNS TTL considered
- rollback ready
- support/on-call ready

After:

- verify data
- verify business flows
- monitor

---

topics.title: Appendix GF — Migration Rollback
topics.markdown:
Rollback may require:

- reverse replication
- write freeze
- reconciliation

If data is written in cloud after cutover, simply pointing DNS back can lose data.

Plan before migration.

---

topics.title: Appendix GG — Hybrid Identity
topics.markdown:
During migration, identity may span:

- on-prem directory
- cloud SSO
- SaaS

Use federation.

Avoid duplicate user lifecycle systems.

---

topics.title: Appendix GH — Hybrid DNS
topics.summary: On-prem must resolve cloud private names and vice versa.
topics.markdown:
On-prem must resolve cloud private names and vice versa.

Configure:

- conditional forwarders
- private zones
- resolver endpoints

DNS is often the hardest hidden hybrid dependency.

---

topics.title: Appendix GI — Hybrid Routing
topics.markdown:
Ensure no CIDR overlap.

Plan:

- route advertisements
- asymmetric paths
- firewall inspection

Document ownership between network teams.

---

topics.title: Appendix GJ — Cloud Exit Strategy
topics.markdown:
For critical provider-specific services, document:

- export format
- data ownership
- migration lead time
- alternative

You do not need immediate portability, but should understand exit cost.

---

topics.title: Appendix GK — Multi-Cloud Networking
topics.markdown:
Connecting clouds introduces:

- VPN/dedicated links
- routing
- DNS
- encryption
- egress cost

Cross-cloud synchronous chatter is often expensive and fragile.

---

topics.title: Appendix GL — Multi-Cloud Identity
topics.summary: Use central identity provider and federation.
topics.markdown:
Use central identity provider and federation.

Avoid separate unmanaged user directories in every cloud.

---

topics.title: Appendix GM — Multi-Cloud Observability
topics.markdown:
Centralize or federate telemetry.

Need common:

- service names
- trace context
- labels
- SLO definitions

Do not let each cloud become an operational silo.

---

topics.title: Appendix GN — Multi-Cloud Data
topics.summary: Replicating data across providers is difficult due to:
topics.markdown:
Replicating data across providers is difficult due to:

- bandwidth
- egress cost
- consistency
- service differences

Use only where business value justifies it.

---

topics.title: Appendix GO — Cloud Operating Roles
topics.markdown:
Common responsibilities:

- cloud platform
- security
- networking
- application teams
- FinOps
- SRE

Define ownership clearly.

---

topics.title: Appendix GP — Platform Team as Product Team
topics.markdown:
Platform customers are developers.

Track:

- adoption
- satisfaction
- lead time
- support burden

Do not build platform features without user demand.

---

topics.title: Appendix GQ — Golden Paths
codeBlocks:
create service
deploy
get DB
get secret
observe
topics.markdown:
Provide standard way to:

```text
create service
deploy
get DB
get secret
observe
```

Defaults should be secure and reliable.

Allow escape hatches for legitimate needs.

---

topics.title: Appendix GR — Platform APIs
topics.summary: Prefer self-service APIs/portals over manual tickets.
topics.markdown:
Prefer self-service APIs/portals over manual tickets.

Automation reduces:

- lead time
- inconsistency
- human error

---

topics.title: Appendix GS — Platform Abstraction Depth
topics.summary: Do not hide every cloud concept.
topics.markdown:
Do not hide every cloud concept.

Developers still need to understand:

- latency
- scaling
- quotas
- failure

A platform should remove repetitive complexity, not obscure reality.

---

topics.title: Appendix GT — Shared Service Blast Radius
topics.markdown:
Central services like:

- auth
- config
- DNS
- secrets
- service discovery

can impact every team.

Design them for:

- high reliability
- graceful degradation
- regional independence

---

topics.title: Appendix GU — Control Plane Independence
topics.summary: Data plane should often continue if control plane temporarily unavailable.
codeBlocks:
config service unavailable
 -> app uses cached last-known-good config
topics.markdown:
Data plane should often continue if control plane temporarily unavailable.

Example:

```text
config service unavailable
 -> app uses cached last-known-good config
```

This reduces global outages.

---

topics.title: Appendix GV — Organization-Wide Observability Platform
topics.markdown:
Provide standard:

- log format
- metrics
- tracing
- dashboards
- SLO tooling

Prevent each team building incompatible telemetry stack.

---

topics.title: Appendix GW — Organization-Wide Identity Platform
topics.markdown:
Central identity should provide:

- workload identity
- user SSO
- token verification
- role standards

Avoid application teams inventing authentication independently.

---

topics.title: Appendix GX — Organization-Wide Network Platform
topics.markdown:
Network platform can provide:

- VPC vending
- DNS
- connectivity
- firewall policy
- private endpoints

Self-service with guardrails is better than ticket-based networking.

---

topics.title: Appendix GY — Cloud Governance at Scale
topics.markdown:
Automate:

- resource inventory
- security posture
- tagging
- budget
- quota
- ownership

Unknown/unowned resources are risk.

---

topics.title: Appendix GZ — Resource Ownership
codeBlocks:
owner
service
environment
purpose
topics.markdown:
Every production resource should have:

```text
owner
service
environment
purpose
```

Ownership enables:

- incident routing
- cost
- lifecycle
- security response

---

topics.title: Appendix HA — Decommissioning
topics.summary: Migration or project is not done until old resources are removed.
topics.markdown:
Migration or project is not done until old resources are removed.

Checklist:

- zero traffic
- zero dependencies
- backup/retention decision
- revoke credentials
- remove DNS
- delete compute
- archive logs
- stop alerts

Dead resources cost money and create risk.

---

topics.title: Appendix HB — Architecture Decision Records
codeBlocks:
# ADR

## Context
## Decision
## Alternatives
## Consequences
## Migration
## Reversal
topics.markdown:
Record important decisions:

```markdown
# ADR

## Context
## Decision
## Alternatives
## Consequences
## Migration
## Reversal
```

Preserve reasoning.

---

topics.title: Appendix HC — Cloud Design Document
topics.markdown:
A strong cloud RFC includes:

1. problem
2. requirements
3. non-goals
4. scale
5. regions
6. network
7. IAM
8. compute
9. storage/data
10. security
11. observability
12. HA/DR
13. cost
14. deployment
15. migration
16. ownership
17. alternatives
18. risks

---

topics.title: Appendix HD — Reversible vs Irreversible Decisions
topics.markdown:
Easy to reverse:

- instance type
- minor autoscaling setting

Hard to reverse:

- region strategy
- partition key
- account hierarchy
- public API
- global data model

Spend more design effort on hard-to-reverse choices.

---

topics.title: Appendix HE — Architecture Risk Register
topics.markdown:
Example:

| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| NAT cost unexpectedly high | Medium | Medium | private endpoints + cost test |
| DB cannot handle peak writes | Medium | High | load test + scaling plan |
| DR restore exceeds RTO | Medium | High | quarterly restore drills |
| IAM role too broad | Medium | High | policy validation |

Make risks explicit.

---
